End-to-end T2 corporate tax return filing for Ontario corporations — every required schedule, every eligible credit, foreign and related-party reporting handled correctly, and year-round support, delivered by a corporate tax accountant at AFFORDABLE flat-fee pricing with no surprise fees.

1

T2 Corporate Return Preparation & Filing

Accurate preparation and electronic filing of your T2 return with all required CRA schedules. The right return depends on your corporation's size and activity — the full T2, the T2 Short, and the schedules that attach all turn on specific tests. We file the correct version with every schedule CRA expects.

  • We determine whether your corporation qualifies for the two-page T2 Short Return, available only to a CCPC with nil or loss income or a tax-exempt corporation, and file the full T2 with complete schedules where it does not.
  • We complete Schedule 9 to report related and associated corporations, the disclosure CRA uses to confirm whether the Small Business Deduction limit must be shared across a corporate group.
  • We file Schedule 11 to report transactions between the corporation and its shareholders, officers, and employees, a related-party disclosure CRA matches against the individuals' personal returns.
  • We prepare the General Index of Financial Information in long form where assets or revenue require it, ensuring the GIFI detail matches the financial statements behind the T2 corporate tax return.
  • We e-file through CRA-certified software with the confirmation recorded, delivering accurate corporate tax return filing at a cost-effective flat fee.
2

CRA Compliance and Correspondence

We manage CRA communication, assessments, and notices to keep your corporation fully compliant. Beyond the annual return, a corporation carries foreign-reporting and information-return obligations that CRA enforces with heavy penalties. We track and file them so compliance is complete, not just the T2.

  • We file Form T1134 for foreign affiliates where the corporation owns 10% or more of a non-resident corporation, meeting the annual disclosure CRA requires within the prescribed deadline after year-end.
  • We file Form T106 to report transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents exceeding the $1 million threshold, the cross-border disclosure CRA penalizes heavily when missed.
  • We report foreign property on Form T1135 where the corporation's specified foreign property cost exceeds $100,000, separate from the income reported on the T2.
  • We review every Notice of Assessment against the filed return, confirming CRA processed the schedules, credits, and instalments as filed before the assessment is accepted.
  • We act on your behalf through Represent a Client, keeping correspondence managed with transparent pricing.
3

Tax Credits and Deductions Optimization

Identification and application of all eligible federal and provincial credits to reduce your tax burden. Credits are claimed on specific schedules with their own rules — claimed wrong, they are denied. We apply each one correctly so your corporation keeps every dollar of credit it has earned.

  • We claim the federal foreign tax credit on Schedule 21 where the corporation earned income taxed abroad, preventing the same income from being taxed twice across jurisdictions.
  • We apply the Ontario corporate tax credits on Schedule 500, including the Ontario small business rate, so the provincial portion of the T2 is calculated correctly.
  • We claim charitable donations on Schedule 2 within the 75% of net income limit, carrying any excess forward over the five-year window available to corporations.
  • We apply political contribution and other minor credits where eligible, each on its prescribed line so CRA accepts the claim without query.
  • We confirm every credit is supported in the working file, delivering the optimization as part of our affordable service.
4

Year-End Review and Tax Strategy

Guidance on improving tax efficiency through proper planning before and after your fiscal year-end. The return reports decisions; the year-end review shapes them. We look at the position just before and just after year-end, where small timing choices change what the T2 ultimately reports.

  • We review whether the corporation should pay a bonus or dividend before year-end to manage the active business income kept under the Small Business Deduction limit on the upcoming return.
  • We confirm the fiscal period does not exceed 53 weeks, the maximum a corporation's tax year may run, and plan the year-end date where a short first year applies.
  • We assess whether the functional currency election suits a corporation reporting mainly in US dollars, allowing the T2 to be filed in that currency where it reduces exchange volatility.
  • We time the realization of income and deductible expenses around the year-end date, so the corporate tax return reflects a planned result rather than an accident of timing.
  • We deliver the review before filing, so the strategy is actionable, with no surprise fees.
5

Back-Filing and Prior Year Adjustments

Support for missed returns, corrections, and adjustments to restore compliance and recover benefits. A missed return often means missed refunds and credits, not just exposure. We file the back years and adjust prior ones to restore standing and recover what the corporation is owed.

  • We file prior-year T2 returns and claim refundable credits that were never received, since a refundable credit such as a refundable ITC can still be recovered when the late return is filed within the allowed period.
  • We recover loss carrybacks from a prior-year filing, applying a current loss against tax already paid up to three years back to generate a refund.
  • We correct a prior return's dividend refund claim through the RDTOH pools where the original filing under-claimed the refund on taxable dividends paid.
  • We confirm the corporation's standing with CRA and the Ontario Business Registry is restored once the back years are filed and accepted.
  • We complete the back-filing affordably, recovering benefits the corporation would otherwise lose.
6

Ongoing Support and Guidance

Year-round assistance to answer tax questions, interpret CRA updates, and keep your corporation prepared for future filings. Tax does not pause between returns. We stay available all year so a question, a CRA letter, or a rule change is handled when it arises, not deferred to filing season.

  • We keep your records and schedules organized between filings, so each year-end starts from a current position rather than a backlog.

Frequently Asked Corporate Tax Return Filing Questions

What is a corporate tax return (T2), and who needs to file it?

A corporate tax return (T2) is a mandatory annual report that every Canadian resident corporation—including Toronto businesses—must file with the CRA, even if no tax is owed. This requirement applies to operating companies, holding companies, and incorporated professionals. The T2 form summarizes your corporation’s income, deductions, and credits for the year, ensuring full compliance and transparency. At Gondaliya CPA, we help businesses prepare and file accurate T2 returns efficiently, giving you peace of mind and confidence in your CRA compliance.

What is the deadline for filing my corporate tax return in Toronto?

You must file your T2 Corporate Tax Return within six months following the end of your corporation’s fiscal year. For example, if your fiscal year closes on December 31, your return is due by June 30. However, any taxes owed are generally payable within two or three months of year-end; late payment can result in interest and penalties, so early filing is recommended.

What documents do I need to provide for my T2 filing?

To file your T2 accurately, you’ll need key documents such as year-end financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement), supporting schedules (GIFI codes), detailed bookkeeping records, bank statements, payroll summaries, receipts for business expenses, and any CRA correspondence. At Gondaliya CPA, we guide you in gathering and organizing all necessary documentation, ensuring your claims are fully supported, maximizing available credits, and keeping your corporation compliant and audit-ready.

Can I file my corporate return electronically, and is it required?

Yes. Since 2024, all Canadian corporations—including those based in Toronto—must file the T2 return electronically unless exempt (for example, certain non-resident or insurance corporations). Failing to e-file when required can result in a $1,000 penalty. Electronic filing is faster, more secure, and preferred by the CRA.

What are common deductions and credits Toronto corporations should claim?

At Gondaliya CPA, we help your corporation claim all eligible deductions, including salaries, rent, utilities, office supplies, professional fees, and vehicle expenses. We also guide you to valuable credits like the Small Business Deduction, SR&ED (Scientific Research & Experimental Development), digital adoption or environmental incentives, and Ontario-specific programs. Our expertise ensures you maximize savings while staying fully compliant.

What happens if my corporation is inactive or has no income?

Even if your corporation had no income or business activity this year, filing a nil T2 return is mandatory. Gondaliya CPA makes this process simple, accurate, and stress-free, helping you avoid penalties and maintain good standing with the CRA.

What is the difference between the T2 and T2 Short return?

The standard T2 return is a 9-page form required for most corporations, while the T2 Short is a simplified 2-page version for eligible single-province businesses not claiming refundable credits or reporting dividends. Gondaliya CPA ensures your corporation files the correct form, minimizing errors and maximizing compliance.

How should I handle late or missed filings?

If a deadline is missed, prompt action is crucial. Gondaliya CPA quickly files overdue T2 returns, communicates with the CRA on your behalf, and minimizes penalties and interest. We also handle multi-year catch-up filings, keeping your business compliant and worry-free.

Accuracy starts with organized, well-supported financial records. Gondaliya CPA reviews every detail, validates receipts, and ensures claimed expenses are reasonable and CRA-compliant. With our expertise, your return is not only accurate but fully audit-ready, giving you confidence and peace of mind.

10 Smart T2 Corporate Tax Return Filing Strategies That Save Money

Meet Your T2 Filing Deadline

Your T2 corporate tax return is due six months after your fiscal year-end, but the tax balance owing is due within two or three months depending on corporation type. Late T2 filing triggers a 5% penalty on unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months. Filing your corporate tax return on time keeps that money in your business.

Claim the Full Small Business Deduction

Schedule 1 of your T2 corporate tax return calculates the Small Business Deduction on the first $500,000 of active business income, taxing it at roughly 12.2% combined federal-Ontario. Failing to review associated corporation relationships under ITA section 256 before T2 filing can cost you up to 17% in extra corporate tax.

Maximize CCA on Schedule 8

Your T2 corporate tax return should claim full capital cost allowance on every eligible asset class through Schedule 8. The Accelerated Investment Incentive allows a first-year write-off on qualifying equipment, vehicles, and technology. Missing CCA deductions on your corporate tax return filing defers tax savings you are legally entitled to claim now.

Map GIFI Codes Accurately

Every line on Schedule 100 and Schedule 125 of your T2 return must map precisely to your trial balance using correct GIFI codes. Misclassified revenue, expenses, or balance sheet items on your corporate tax return filing trigger CRA matching errors and review letters within weeks. Accurate GIFI mapping prevents unnecessary scrutiny of your T2.

Reconcile Shareholder Loans on Schedule 50

Your T2 corporate tax return must report every shareholder loan accurately on Schedule 50. Under ITA subsection 15(2), unpaid shareholder loans become taxable personal income if not repaid within one year of your corporation's fiscal year-end. Proper reporting during T2 filing avoids this costly reassessment on amounts you already returned.

File T2 Electronically Every Year

Corporations with gross revenue over $1 million must e-file their T2 corporate tax return — paper filing triggers a $100 penalty per return. Even below that threshold, electronic T2 filing through CRA's internet filing service gets faster acknowledgment, reduces processing errors, and confirms your corporate tax return was received without postal delays.

Use Loss Carrybacks on Schedule 4

If your T2 corporate tax return shows a non-capital loss this year, Schedule 4 lets you carry it back three years and recover corporate tax already paid to CRA. Losses also carry forward 20 years on future T2 filings. This is real cash refunded directly to your corporation from prior corporate tax return filings.

Track the Capital Dividend Account

Your T2 corporate tax return should reconcile the Capital Dividend Account balance after every capital gain, life insurance proceeds, or eligible capital property disposition. Filing Form T2054 alongside your corporate tax return lets you distribute these amounts completely tax-free to shareholders. Ignoring the CDA on your T2 filing means shareholders pay personal tax they never owed.

Review Associated Corporation Allocations

If your corporation is associated with others under ITA section 256, Schedule 23 of each T2 corporate tax return must show a consistent SBD allocation across the group. Filing corporate tax returns with conflicting allocations triggers CRA reassessments and compound interest on the resulting shortfall. We coordinate every associated T2 filing to prevent this.

Declare Year-End Bonuses Strategically

If your T2 corporate tax return shows higher-than-expected income, declare a management bonus before fiscal year-end and pay it within 179 days. The bonus is deductible on your corporate tax return filing in the current year while deferring personal tax to the next calendar year. This T2 strategy legally shifts income across two periods.
